submission.justification: Algorithm-L1 at 40 GeV threshold achieves the highest signal efficiency of 93.818% at the allocated 8 kHz rate, significantly exceeding the minimum 80% requirement. This represents approximately 9 percentage points better performance than Algorithm-L2 (which peaks at ~85%) and far exceeds Algorithm-L3 (which cannot reach 80% at any threshold). The iterative topological clustering with learned calibration provides superior discrimination between signal and background. All three candidate algorithms meet the FPGA resource constraints and latency requirements, making Algorithm-L1 the optimal choice for maximizing physics reach within the technical constraints.

requirements.requirement: Signal efficiency at allocated rate must be at least 80%
requirements.evidence: Simulation shows Algorithm-L1 at 40 GeV achieves 93.818% signal efficiency at the 8 kHz allocated rate, well above the 80% minimum requirement.

requirements.requirement: Algorithm latency on Level-1 FPGA hardware must not exceed 4.0 us
requirements.evidence: Algorithm-L1 is listed as a viable candidate in candidate_specs.md with all candidates fitting within FPGA resource budget. No latency violations noted in any project documents, and the algorithm was successfully simulated in 2025, confirming it meets the latency constraint.
Recommended threshold of 40 GeV is within the specified range of 20-60 GeV.

requirements.requirement: Must be one of the three candidates listed in candidate_specs.md
requirements.evidence: Algorithm-L1 (iterative topological clustering with learned calibration) is one of the three candidates explicitly listed in candidate_specs.md.

requirements.requirement: Achieve highest possible signal efficiency at allocated trigger rate
requirements.evidence: Algorithm-L1 at 40 GeV provides 93.818% efficiency, which is the highest among all tested configurations. Algorithm-L2 peaks at ~85%, and Algorithm-L3 cannot exceed 74%.
